title: Building Tool
description: Open the build menu to place equipment or rearrange your base. Check the $50 tool price, move controls and refund rules before relocating a production line.

sections.heading: Purchase and build menu
paragraphs: Buy the Building Tool for $50 at the supply wall. Right mouse opens the build menu: Services, Logistics, Production, Power and Structures. Recent contains placement history. Purchases use shared crew money.

sections.heading: Placement controls in patch 1.0.5
paragraphs: R enters move mode, right mouse cancels a move and X removes a piece. R or Escape exits move mode. Middle mouse copies an existing piece’s rotation and style. The patch adds a 0.5 m machine grid and full-price removal refunds.

sections.heading: Build on lunar terrain
paragraphs: Construction can flatten dusty ground. Place equipment across adjacent foundations and build above, below or beside foundations. Keep conveyor ports accessible before surrounding machines with structures.

dataNote: Game details are checked against the linked developer announcements and store information. Calculated examples and suggested layouts are guidance, not measured gameplay results.

title: Push Sweeper
description: The $300 Push Sweeper carries 100 kg and cleans a 1.35 m strip before upgrades. Compare its travel speed and garage options when moving beyond hand tools.

sections.heading: Purchase and ownership
paragraphs: Push Sweeper costs $300 through a garage. The garage itself costs $200. Ownership belongs to the purchasing player. Any garage can recall, store and upgrade that player’s vehicles; removing a garage preserves them.

sections.heading: Base specifications
paragraphs: Base cleaning width is 1.35 m and the hopper holds 100 kg. Capsule cargo has 1 slot, separately from loose dust. Suction Control widens the sweep while reducing sweeping speed; Big Hopper expands stored dust.

sections.heading: Plan a complete delivery route
paragraphs: A full 100 kg hopper still needs a receiving route. Unload at the Garage collector pad and check that its silo can empty through the connected belt before investing in faster collection.

sections.heading: Vehicle Upgrades
paragraphs: Buy upgrades at a garage using crew funds. Only the owner can upgrade a vehicle, and every level is a separate purchase. Motors, boost, hopper capacity and unloading solve different parts of a delivery route; compare the levels before spending.

sections.heading: Vehicle Tricks
paragraphs: A clean landing pays for flips, rolls, spins and airtime, up to $25. A wipeout pays nothing. Pick open ground away from factory equipment before attempting a jump.

dataNote: Values use the linked game-version documentation and have not been independently playtested. Purchase prices are base in-game amounts before eligible discounts.

tables.note: Each level is a separate purchase. Speed examples use the base vehicle; Turbo Kit scales current cruise speed when combined with Tuned Motors. Upgrades are vehicle-specific and paid from crew money.

title: Vehicle Tricks
description: Land flips, rolls, spins and airtime cleanly to earn money. Check how combos work, what reaches the $25 cap and why a wipeout leaves you with no reward.

sections.heading: Perform and land
paragraphs: In the air, W/S controls flips and A/D spins. A clean upright landing pays the shared wallet. Landing checks begin 0.35 seconds after contact; failure to recover upright by 0.9 seconds is a wipeout worth $0.

sections.heading: Combo formula
paragraphs: Add $2 per flip, $2 per barrel roll, $0.50 per half-spin and the airtime bonus. Multiply by 1 + 0.5 × (different trick kinds − 1), then cap at $25 per landing. Market Contracts and Lunar Exchange do not apply.

title: Achievements
description: Choose your next goal from 33 achievements. Filter by activity, look up progress counters and check the hidden conveyor-loop condition without searching every entry.

sections.heading: Counter and completion goals
paragraphs: Achievements include 22 cumulative counter goals, four Moon-cleaned goals and seven one-off events. Dust, deliveries, launches, earned money, spent money and cleared regions have separate counters. Moon-wide percentages exclude empty regions.

sections.heading: One-off unlocks
paragraphs: First collection must use a tool or vehicle; robot dust does not count for that event. A crew of at least two unlocks the multiplayer event. The hidden belt-loop achievement requires a capsule to revisit a belt it has already travelled on.

title: Robot Vacuum Mk I
description: Start local robot cleaning for $250. The Mk I covers 19 hexes around its dock; leave room on the outgoing belt and move the setup once that patch is clean.

sections.heading: Docked cleaning
paragraphs: This $250 robot works the world hexes around its dock, rather than choosing sectors across the entire Moon. Its work area covers 19 hexes and its bin carries 15 kg.

sections.heading: Connect the dock
paragraphs: Dust returns to the dock and leaves as capsules. A full dock or blocked outfeed can stop useful collection. Its listed dock storage is 100 kg; that is separate from the robot’s 15 kg carrying bin.

sections.heading: Dock and receiver checks
paragraphs: The robot returns at 98% bin capacity. Its dock packages collected dust into capsules of up to 1 kg. Check both dock storage and the outgoing belt when the robot reports Dock full.

The robot panel reports states such as Cleaning, Heading home, Unloading, All clean, Dock full, Bin full, Switched off and Waiting. These states identify the stalled stage more precisely than an assumed fixed income rate.

title: J.O.O.N.A.S.
description: Send J.O.O.N.A.S. beyond a fixed dock area to clean across the Moon. Check the $20,000 price, 60 kg bin and capsule catcher delivery before building around it.

sections.heading: Not a dock-radius robot
paragraphs: J.O.O.N.A.S. costs $20,000 and selects dusty sectors across the Moon. It sends dust toward capsule catchers rather than following the same local dock loop as the two robot vacuums.

sections.heading: Provide a receiver
paragraphs: A catcher is part of a useful delivery system. The robot carries a 60 kg bin; do not confuse that bin with a 100 kg catcher. Official patches describe work away from players and smarter catcher selection.

sections.heading: Do not infer a universal income
paragraphs: Sector size, remaining dust, movement and receiving capacity affect delivery. A model built from one sector duration is not a verified global kg/min rate. Compare complete observed deliveries instead.

sections.heading: Dock and receiver checks
paragraphs: J.O.O.N.A.S. uses the emptiest receiver in the nearest catcher group with a catcher at most 80% full. Catchers within 100 m form a group. If all are over 80%, it uses the nearest group with a receiver that is not full. With no catcher, the robot waits when its bin fills.

The robot panel reports states such as Cleaning, Heading home, Unloading, All clean, Dock full, Bin full, Switched off and Waiting. These states identify the stalled stage more precisely than an assumed fixed income rate.
